## Container model

**Image and Dockerfile**

- Image tag: `charliehub/transit-manager:latest`
- Dockerfile: `/opt/charliehub/transit-manager/Dockerfile`
- Build flow:
  - `FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm`
  - Install `openssh-client`, `wireguard-tools`, `android-tools-adb`
  - `WORKDIR /app`
  - `COPY requirements.txt .` then `pip install`
  - `COPY app/ ./`  ← the layer that rebuilds on any source edit
  - Runtime user: `appuser` (UID 1000)
  - `CMD uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8010` — no `--reload`

**Critical**: the app source is `COPY`'d at image build time, **not
bind-mounted**. Host edits to `app/**/*.py` do NOT propagate to the
running container. A code change requires rebuilding the image and
recreating the container.

**Bind mounts** (read-only — the only live host→container channels):

| Source on host | Destination in container | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/opt/charliehub/secrets/transit_id_ed25519` | `/home/appuser/.ssh/transit_id_ed25519` | deploy SSH key |
| `/opt/charliehub/secrets/transit_peer_id_ed25519` | `/home/appuser/.ssh/transit_peer_id_ed25519` | restricted peer SSH key |
| `/opt/charliehub/secrets/charliehub-internal-ca.crt` | `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/charliehub-internal-ca.crt` | internal CA cert |
| `/opt/charliehub/transit-core/transit-dispatch.sh` | `/etc/charliehub/canonical/transit-dispatch.sh` | dispatcher source for SHA compare |

**Compose**

- Project: `transit-manager`
- File: `/opt/charliehub/transit-manager/docker-compose.yml`
- Service: `transit-manager`
- Container name: `charliehub_transit_manager`
- Port: `127.0.0.1:8010 → 8010`
- Networks: `net-backend`, `net-data`, `net-observability` (all external)
- Healthcheck: HTTP `GET /health`, 30s interval, 30s start-period

## Modifying source / deploying changes

Standard flow for a Python edit. Single sudo prompt at the start
if you script it as `sudo -u ubuntu bash <script>`.

```
# 1. Edit on host (ubuntu owns the source tree)
sudo -u ubuntu vim /opt/charliehub/transit-manager/app/services/transit_generator.py

# 2. Pin the current image for rollback
docker tag charliehub/transit-manager:latest \
  charliehub/transit-manager:pre-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)

# 3. Rebuild — only the app/ COPY layer rebuilds, ~5–15s
cd /opt/charliehub/transit-manager
BUILD_TIMESTAMP="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
  docker compose build transit-manager

# 4. Recreate the container atomically
docker compose up -d --force-recreate --no-deps transit-manager

# 5. Wait for healthy (start-period is 30s, budget 60s)
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  s=$(docker inspect charliehub_transit_manager --format '{{.State.Health.Status}}')
  printf "t+%ds  health=%s\n" $((i*2)) "$s"
  [ "$s" = healthy ] && break
  sleep 2
done
```

**Outage window**: ~10–30s during step 4 (stop + remove + create
+ start). `transit-mcp` and any in-flight `deploy-transit.sh` calls
will see transient connection errors in that window.

**Rollback** (if step 5 fails or behavior is wrong):

```
docker tag charliehub/transit-manager:pre-<TS> charliehub/transit-manager:latest
cd /opt/charliehub/transit-manager
docker compose up -d --force-recreate --no-deps transit-manager
# also restore host source if you edited there:
cp /path/to/<file>.py.pre-<TAG>.<TS> /path/to/<file>.py
```

## Migrations

Numbered SQL files in `/opt/charliehub/transit-manager/migrations/NNN_<topic>.sql`.

**Migration runner: `scripts/migrate_schema.py`** (introduced A12, SD-WAN v4.5 —
this page previously said "no migration runner"; that was true before A12 and is
no longer accurate). Applies pending files in filename order, tracked in a
self-managed `public.schema_migrations` ledger (checksum-recorded per file, shared
with domain-manager since both live in the one physical `charliehub_domains`
database). Full detail, including the ledger schema and migration-history
reconciliation work: [Schema Migrations](../control-plane/specs/schema-migrations.md).

```
DB_HOST=... DB_NAME=... DB_USER=... DB_PASS=... \
  python3 scripts/migrate_schema.py transit-manager [--dry-run | --status | --only <N> | --rollback N]
```

- `--status` / `--dry-run` — read-only / preview.
- `--only <N>` (added 2026-07-12, alongside the edge-convergence increment-2
  fabric-charter work) — apply exactly **one** named pending migration and leave
  the rest of the pending set untouched. The correct tool whenever other pending
  files are out of scope for the current change — e.g. applying `078` without
  also sweeping in unrelated `075` or the deliberately-held `076`.
- `--rollback N` — unwind the last N applied migrations, pre-flight-checked
  against missing rollback scripts.

**Connectivity on hub2:** the runner's plain `DB_HOST=...` TCP path cannot reach
the DB as the owning superuser on hub2 (documented connectivity gap — see
[Schema Migrations § Applying migrations on live hub2](../control-plane/specs/schema-migrations.md)).
Verified working interim procedure (2026-07-12, used to apply `078`):
`docker run --network container:charliehub-postgres ...` — sharing the postgres
container's network namespace so `127.0.0.1` inside the ephemeral runner
container hits the same local-trust `pg_hba.conf` rule a container-local `psql`
gets. This lets the **actual runner** — not manual `psql` — apply the file and
record the ledger row automatically (correct checksum, no hand-typed SQL
`INSERT`). Still doesn't fix the underlying `.env`↔live-role credential mismatch
(that's the tracked B7/B11 work), but it is materially safer than the
manual-apply-plus-hand-insert-ledger-row procedure it supersedes as the interim
path.

Idempotency conventions used by existing migrations:

- Enum extensions: `DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS` then `ADD CONSTRAINT`
- New columns: `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`
- New tables: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`

Schema lives in the `transit` schema of the `charliehub_domains`
database. See [Transit Manager Schema](transit-manager-schema.md)
for column inventory.

## API surface — what is mutable

The `routers/interfaces.py` PUT endpoint exposes only a small
allowlist via the `InterfaceUpdate` Pydantic model:

```python
class InterfaceUpdate(BaseModel):
    """Only non-structural fields are mutable after creation."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    status:       Optional[str] = None
    geo_table_id: Optional[int] = None
    notes:        Optional[str] = None
```

`extra="forbid"` means any field NOT in the allowlist is rejected.
This is intentional — structural fields are not API-mutable:

- `interface_type` — schema-class signal; changing affects render gate
- `address`, `listen_port`, `private_key_ref` — interface identity
- `name` — primary identifier

Structural changes require a migration (for enum extensions) plus a
guarded `psql` UPDATE (break-glass) in a transaction with an end-state
guard. The break-glass pattern is: capture pre-state, guarded UPDATE
with current-state predicate, end-state DO block raising on mismatch,
COMMIT, audit log entry referencing the migration or doctrine page.

`routers/peers.py` exposes more flexibility (peer activate/disable,
geo changes); consult that module for the current allowlist.

## Two SSH keys for transit-core

Transit Manager talks to ch-transit-core (the WireGuard transit VM
at `10.0.0.2`) over two SSH identities, both gated by `ForceCommand`
wrappers that constrain what each key can do.

| Key | Host path | ForceCommand on VM | Allowed verbs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Deploy key** | `/opt/charliehub/secrets/transit_id_ed25519` | `transit-dispatch.sh` | `__sync_interface__ <iface>`, `__sync_rules__`, `__reload_nft__`, `__rollback__`, `__healthcheck_dispatch__`, empty → `apply-transit.sh` (stdin = JSON payload) |
| **Peer key** | `/opt/charliehub/secrets/transit_peer_id_ed25519` | `transit-wrapper.sh` | `wg show dump`, `peer-route-set`, `peer-route-clear`, `ip rule list`, drift-monitor reads |

The canonical dispatcher source on hub2 is
`/opt/charliehub/transit-core/transit-dispatch.sh`. The TM container
bind-mounts it read-only and computes its SHA256 at module import
time (`peer_vm_sync.probe_dispatcher_syncable`); the value is compared
against what the VM advertises via `__healthcheck_dispatch__`. Drift
fails `charliehub_dispatcher_hash_match=0` and is alertable.

Publishing a new dispatcher: `/opt/charliehub/scripts/publish-transit-dispatch.sh`.

## Deploy orchestration

The in-process `POST /api/transit/deploy` was rebuilt as the **S1 scoped deploy** (S1.3, 2026-05-28): body `{scope, dry_run}`, sole writer of `edge_node_status`. The host-orchestrated `deploy-transit.sh` remains the full-fabric path.

```
POST /api/transit/render
       │   ← pure function of DB intent; no SSH, no writes; returns JSON
       ▼
/opt/charliehub/scripts/deploy-transit.sh
       │   ← orchestrator: validation, dispatcher pre-flight, per-node SSH
       ▼
For each node in apply_order:
  ssh -i <DEPLOY_KEY> <node>   ← payload over stdin
       │
       ▼
  transit-dispatch.sh (ForceCommand on transit-core)
       │
       ▼
  apply-transit.sh (transit-core) or apply-transit-edge.sh (edge)
```

`deploy-transit.sh` also:

- Validates min checksum count and absence of raw private keys in the render payload
- Pre-flight dispatcher SHA healthcheck (refuses to apply on drift)
- Per-node WAN path check for TRANSPORT_RISKY transports (deadlock guard)
- Post-deploy convergence wait + fabric assertion (can trigger global rollback)
- CCM edge reconciliation hook

**Scripts**

| Script | Lives on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/opt/charliehub/scripts/deploy-transit.sh` | hub2 | main deploy orchestrator |
| `/opt/charliehub/scripts/apply-transit-edge.sh` | hub2 (scp'd to edges per deploy) | per-edge apply |
| `/opt/charliehub/scripts/apply-transit.sh` | **transit-core only** | invoked via SSH `ForceCommand`; not present on hub2 |
| `/opt/charliehub/scripts/publish-transit-dispatch.sh` | hub2 | publishes canonical dispatcher to transit-core |

### Invocation

Canonical command (works as charles, since charles is allowed to
`sudo -u ubuntu` general commands):

```
sudo -u ubuntu bash /opt/charliehub/scripts/deploy-transit.sh
```

**The `bash` prefix is required, not optional.** The script is
checked in at mode `0664` (`-rw-rw-r-- ubuntu:ubuntu`) — no
execute bit — so `sudo -u ubuntu /opt/.../deploy-transit.sh`
fails with `command not found` (it is sudo's way of reporting
an `execve` refusal, not a missing file). Invoking through
`bash <path>` only requires read permission, which is what
ubuntu has.

**Run as `ubuntu`, not root**, because the script:

- sources `/opt/charliehub/.env` (env vars + API keys, ubuntu-readable)
- uses the deploy SSH key at `/opt/charliehub/secrets/transit_id_ed25519`
- contains an inner `sudo /opt/charliehub/scripts/check_transit_fabric.sh --quick`
  that relies on **ubuntu having NOPASSWD** for that specific binary
  in `/etc/sudoers.d/`. If that NOPASSWD rule is missing, the
  fabric assertion at the end of the deploy will prompt for
  ubuntu's password and stall.

Dry-run (skips per-node SSH apply; useful to validate the render
payload without touching the fabric):

```
sudo -u ubuntu bash /opt/charliehub/scripts/deploy-transit.sh --dry-run
```

#### Common failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `sudo: /opt/.../deploy-transit.sh: command not found` | invoked path directly; the file has no exec bit | use `bash <path>` |
| `sudo: deploy-transit.sh: command not found` when run as charles | charles cannot `sudo <abs-path>` for unallowlisted commands | switch to `sudo -u ubuntu bash <path>` |
| immediate exit (`rc=1`, 0–5 s), no `[deploy-transit] ...` lines | `.env` missing, `TRANSIT_MANAGER_API_KEY` unset, or TM container down | check `docker ps \| grep transit-manager` and `grep TRANSIT_MANAGER_API_KEY /opt/charliehub/.env` (as ubuntu) |
| stalls at `[sudo] password for ubuntu:` mid-deploy | missing NOPASSWD entry for ubuntu on `check_transit_fabric.sh` | add the sudoers rule in `/etc/sudoers.d/` |
| `[deploy-transit] ERROR: dispatcher drift` | canonical `transit-dispatch.sh` SHA on hub2 doesn't match what transit-core advertises | `sudo -u ubuntu /opt/charliehub/scripts/publish-transit-dispatch.sh`, then re-run |

## Worked example — I-IFACE-CLASS-1 implementation (2026-05-18)

End-to-end example of a TM change that touched doctrine, schema,
data, and code. Concretizes the abstract flows above.

**Note:** this example predates the A12 migration runner (introduced
later) — the manual `psql` apply shown below reflects practice *at the
time*, not the current recommended path. See [Migrations](#migrations)
above for how a schema migration is applied today.

**Doctrine** (Phase 1): [I-IFACE-CLASS-1](../control-plane/invariants/i-iface-class-1.md)
and [I-IFACE-HEALTH-1](../control-plane/invariants/i-iface-health-1.md) published via Docs API. Established that
appliance-realized interfaces (e.g. wg-us / UCG Rock) must be
excluded from TM render/deploy and observed via a separate path.

**Schema migration** (Phase 2) — `migrations/036_imported_iface.sql`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE transit.interfaces
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS interfaces_interface_type_check;

ALTER TABLE transit.interfaces
  ADD CONSTRAINT interfaces_interface_type_check
  CHECK (interface_type IN
    ('site','rw','outpost','infra','wan','fabric','imported'));
```

Applied via `sudo cat ... | sudo docker exec -i charliehub-postgres
psql ...` (no migration runner existed yet at this point — manual apply).

**Data update** (Phase 3) — break-glass for wg-us. `interface_type`
is not API-mutable (`InterfaceUpdate` rejects it via `extra="forbid"`),
so direct `psql` was required:

```sql
BEGIN;
UPDATE transit.interfaces
   SET interface_type = 'imported'
 WHERE id = 8 AND name = 'wg-us' AND interface_type = 'site'
RETURNING id, name, interface_type, revision;

DO $$ BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM transit.interfaces
                 WHERE id=8 AND name='wg-us' AND interface_type='imported') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'guard failed';
  END IF;
END $$;
COMMIT;
```

Audit entry appended to `/var/log/charliehub/break-glass-access.log`
with `follow_up=` pointing at the code change (next phase).

**Renderer change** (Phase 4a) — `app/services/transit_generator.py`:

```python
# 1. WireGuard configs (generator_managed only;
#    imported interfaces are appliance-realized; I-IFACE-CLASS-1)
for iface in interfaces:
    if iface.get("interface_type") == "imported":
        continue  # I-IFACE-CLASS-1
    if not iface.get("generator_managed", True):
        continue
    ...
```

Then `docker compose build transit-manager` and
`docker compose up -d --force-recreate --no-deps transit-manager`
per the "Modifying source" flow above.

**Acceptance gate** — render starvation falsification test (this
is the I-IFACE-CLASS-1 invariant test, runnable from hub2):

```
. /opt/charliehub/.env
curl -sf -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/api/transit/render \
  -H "X-API-Key: $TRANSIT_MANAGER_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.nodes["transit-core"].wg | keys[]'
```

Output must NOT contain `wg-us`. Any iface row with
`interface_type='imported'` in `transit.interfaces WHERE status='active'`
must be absent. If one appears, the invariant is broken and the
renderer needs auditing.

This is the authoritative reference for the `transit.*` PostgreSQL schema and all Transit Manager API routes.
For architecture rationale and operational procedures, see:

- [Transit Fabric](../network/transit/transit-fabric.md) — transport layer, WireGuard topology, addressing

## Database: `charliehub_domains` → `transit.*` schema

Transit Manager is the sole writer to this schema. All tables live in the `transit` schema
of the shared `charliehub_domains` PostgreSQL instance (container: `charliehub-postgres`).

No application-level foreign key constraints are enforced — referential integrity is
maintained by the API layer (create/delete ordering). This is by design: it allows
declare-first, commission-second patterns (e.g. register an edge node before its WireGuard
keys are generated).
---

## Three-Layer GEO Model

The transit schema separates GEO concerns across three distinct layers. They share the
`geo_table_id` integer as a join key, but represent different concerns:

| Layer | Table | Meaning |
|-------|-------|---------| 
| Transport | `transit.interfaces` | Which WireGuard interface carries packets for this geo domain |
| Execution | `transit.geo_executors` | Which edge node serves as executor for this geo domain |
| Consumer intent | `transit.peers` / `transit.routing_overrides` | Which geo domain a given client wants to exit via |

These are not the same concept. An `interfaces` row defines the *carrier*; a
`geo_executors` row defines the *executor*; a `peers.geo` value defines the *intent*.
The `geo_table_id` integer (201=uk, 202=fr, 203=us, 204=ad) ties all three together.

Do not confuse `peers.geo` (consumer intent) with `interfaces.geo_table_id` (transport
carrier assignment) — they happen to correlate today, but the model is designed so
that changing the executor does not require changing every peer's geo.

---

## Table Reference

| `status` | text | `'planned'` | NO | `planned` \| `active` |

### `transit.site_subnets`

CIDR subnets belonging to each site. Uses a GiST index (`inet_ops`) to enforce no-overlap.

| Column | Type | Default | Nullable |
|--------|------|---------|----------|
| `id` | integer | serial | NO |
| `site_id` | integer | — | NO |
| `subnet` | cidr | — | NO |

**Constraint:** `no_overlapping_subnets` — GiST index prevents any two subnets from overlapping.

---

### `transit.geos`

Canonical GEO identity table — the single durable source for the tuple
`{table_id, code, table_name}`. Introduced by migration 037 to sever the hidden-mapping
seam that was previously mirrored across `transit_constants.GEO_TABLE_NAMES_BY_ID` (Python),
`v_geo_executor_pool`'s inline CASE, and per-row text in `transit.execution_paths.geo`.

Per **I-GEO-CONSISTENCY-1**: every `geo_table_id` referenced anywhere in `transit.*` MUST
round-trip through this table. The migration enforces this at apply time; TM enforces it
again at boot via `assert_geo_consistency()` in `app/services/geo_registry.py`. Inline
`CHECK (table_id IN 201..204)` constraints on referencing tables remain as defence-in-depth.

**Identity-key choice:** `table_id` (integer) is the PRIMARY KEY because every operational

| table_id | code | table_name | status |
|----------|------|------------|--------|
| 201 | uk | geo-uk | active |
| 202 | fr | geo-fr | active |
| 203 | us | geo-us | active |

#### Mutation audit boundary (verified live 2026-07-20)

The allowed audit vocabulary is **enforced by the database**, not merely described:

```sql
CHECK (target_type = ANY (ARRAY['ip','mac','peer','vpn_user','vpn_invite']))
```

Verified by reading `pg_constraint` and by exercising the constraint with positive and
negative controls inside rolled-back transactions: `site` and `edge` are **rejected** by
`network_actions_log_target_type_check`; `peer` and `vpn_invite` are **accepted**. A
mutation outside this vocabulary cannot be written here even if calling code attempts it —
the write fails at the database.

**Permitted is not exercised.** Recent data covers `peer`, `vpn_user`, `mac` and `ip`.
`vpn_invite` is permitted but was **not observed** in current data. Three distinctions
matter when reasoning about coverage:

- permitted does not mean exercised — an allowed value may have no code path writing it;
- unexercised does not prove a functioning audit path — absence of rows is not evidence
  that the path works and merely had nothing to record;
- rejected target classes cannot be audited through this table at all — for them the
  question of exercise never arises.

**Current audit boundary, stated precisely:** `site`, `edge`, `interface`, `policy` and
DHCP mutation classes have **no audit surface in `network_actions_log` under the current
schema**. This is a structural property of the allowed vocabulary, not a gap in
instrumentation.

**Keep the layers separate:**

| Layer | Role here |
|---|---|
| Enforcement | The database CHECK enforces the allowed audit vocabulary |
| Audit | The table records entity-level mutation events for permitted types |
| Observability | Unaffected — this table is not a telemetry or metrics path |

This is an **audit-coverage** finding only. It does not imply a telemetry or metrics
failure and must not be cited as one. Tracked as an implementation item in the
documentation-consolidation discovered-issues register
(`programme/docs-consolidation/discovered-issues.md`, a repository file, not a published
page).

`routing_drift` is read directly from the in-process `drift_state.transit_drift_state`

**Doctrine (I-PEER-LIFECYCLE-REUSE-1):** `transit.peers.class` and
`transit.interfaces.plane` are orthogonal dimensions — one must never be derived from the
other. The Topology view is about interfaces and their planes; the Peers & VPN view
(`GET /network/api/peers`, live as of B11/B8 remainder, 2026-07-05 — see the read-model
table above) is about peers and their lifecycle ownership, and filters on `p.class` only,
never joining or deriving from `interfaces.plane`. `wg-rw` (identity plane) is a single
interface serving two different peer classes (`rw` and `outpost`) — the read-model's `rw`
peer-group node (Topology view) reflects that merge explicitly rather than inventing a
one-to-one interface↔class mapping, while the Peers view surfaces `rw` and `outpost` as
the two independent classes they are.

`network_vpn_proxy` / `network_transit_proxy` already rely on for this exact host+path
family; `console.py`'s `_require_console_session` dependency reuses it (401 with no
`Remote-User`) rather than inventing a session/cookie model. This is intentionally a
*different* boundary from the JSON API's `X-API-Key` model — that one exists because
`/network/api/*`/`/api/transit/*` are reachable by non-browser callers that never touch
Authelia, and per that dependency's own doctrine comment, `Remote-User` must never be
substituted for a real key there. No role tiering is applied to the console (unlike the
vpn/transit proxies' full-vs-read-only key split, which exists because those proxies can
mutate) — every view here is read-only and the domain has no `allowed_groups` restriction,
so any authenticated user already reaches this host.

**In-process read-model calls.** Each view calls the corresponding `readmodel.py` async
function directly (e.g. `readmodel.overview(scope=scope, auth=True)`) instead of the
review harness's `httpx.get()` round-trip to itself — unnecessary now that the console
lives inside transit-manager. `auth=True` is a literal, not a real key: `Depends(
verify_api_key)` only resolves through FastAPI's own request-dispatch machinery, and
`console.py` has already authenticated the request via `_require_console_session` above
(the correct boundary for *its* transport) before making the call — none of `readmodel.py`'s
handler bodies use the `auth` value for anything beyond satisfying that `Depends()`.
`?scope=`/`?class=` query params on `/network/`, `/network/topology`, `/network/clients`,
and `/network/peers` are forwarded straight to the read-model (its own 400-on-unknown-value
validation applies unchanged) — satisfying E2's "sort/search/scope hit the server-side
read-model params" acceptance item without any template change.

**One genuine template bug fixed (not a template *content* change — a robustness fix):**
`servers.html`'s KPI cards and per-row storage bar assumed every server's
`storage_used_gb`/`storage_total_gb` are always numeric. They are not — see this doc's own
gap note above ("`/network/api/servers` cannot reach px1/px2/px3/vps3/px5 from inside the
deployed container today"): a server the cache cannot reach ships `null` for both fields,
honestly, by design. Jinja's `sum(attribute=)` raises `TypeError` on `int + None`, which
500'd the *entire* Servers view the moment any one server was in that (real, expected,
already-documented) state. Fixed with `rejectattr(..., 'none')` on the two KPI aggregates
and a `have_storage` guard on the per-row bar (rendering `—`, matching the row's existing
Ceph-column convention) — the endpoint's honest-null behaviour is unchanged; only the
template's handling of it was fragile.

**Static assets.** `charliehub-ui-kit/` (Deep Harbour tokens/components/macros, sdwan-v4.5
E1) is baked into the image via a second named build context (`kit`, alongside the existing
`frontend` context for the SPA) — see `transit-manager/docker-compose.yml`
`build.additional_contexts` and the Dockerfile's `COPY --from=kit` stage — rather than
bind-mounted, so a clean image build stays self-contained (same rationale as the SPA's own
`NETWORK-UI-DEPLOY-GAP` fix). `CHARLIEHUB_UI_KIT_DIR` (env, defaulted in the image) points
`console.py`'s Jinja loader and `main.py`'s `/static/kit` mount at it. Mount order in
`main.py` is deliberate: `/static/kit` (narrow) is mounted **before** `/static` (broad,
this app's own `console.css`) — Starlette's `Mount` hands the whole request to the first
registered mount whose path prefix matches, with no fallthrough on a 404, so the reverse
order would make `/static/kit/*` permanently unreachable. (`vpn-spa-v2/app/main.py` mounts
these in the *other* order, which looks like exactly this latent bug — not fixed here, out
of E2's scope, and that app's kit integration is its own comment's "never deployed by this
ticket," so nothing in prod depends on it today. Flagged for whoever picks up vpn-spa-v2's
kit wiring.) `jinja2>=3.1.0` added to `transit-manager/requirements.txt` (same floor
version vpn-spa-v2 pins).

## Key Design Notes

### Generator Purity
`transit_generator.py` and `edge_config_generator.py` are pure functions of the DB state.
No cross-service calls at render time. CCM pre-renders to DB first; TM reads DB only.
Violating this causes render-time side effects that break determinism and drift detection.

### Immutable Fields
Several fields are immutable after creation to preserve cryptographic and topological
integrity. These require delete + recreate:
- `edge_nodes`: `hostname`, `site_id`, `wg_site_address`, `node_role`
- `edge_ingress_vlans`: `vlan_id`, `vlan_iface`, `vlan_subnet`, `vlan_ingress_address`, `lan_subnet`, `lan_egress_iface`, `routing_table_main`, `routing_table_return`, `profile_name`
- `interfaces`: all structural fields (name, address, listen_port, interface_type)

### Revision Tracking
Most tables carry a `revision` integer incremented on each write. The generator uses
revision-based hash comparison to determine whether a stanza has changed since last apply
(avoiding spurious `ifdown` + `ifup` cycles on deploy)

### The `Timestamp:` Header Problem
Stanza comparison must **exclude** the `# Timestamp:` header line — it changes on every
render even when the functional config is identical, which would otherwise trigger false
restarts on every edge deploy. See `apply-transit-edge.sh` for the exclusion logic.

### Execution Certification Gate
An edge node with `execution_capable=false` cannot be used as a GEO executor.
`certify-execution` is the only path to set `execution_capable=true`, requiring:
1. `wan_type` must be set on the node
2. A named `certified_by` and optional `validation_run_id`
This gate was introduced after the I-EXEC-SYMMETRY-1 incident class.

### Retired Address Pools (I-ADDR-1)
`10.244.250.0/24` and `10.244.251.0/24` are retired RW/outpost pools. The API hard-rejects
any new peer whose `allowed_ips` overlaps these ranges. New RW peers must use `10.99.0.0/16`.

[I-GEO-CONSUMER-1](../../control-plane/invariants/i-geo-consumer-1.md));
RW peers (10.99/16) and TVs share the same `geo_policy.apply_exit`
entrypoint. Realization is edge-local for `execution_mode='local'`
overrides (pref-50 rules on the ingress edge) with transit-core
central fallback for `execution_mode='central'`
(per [I-GEO-FAILSAFE-1](../../control-plane/invariants/i-geo-failsafe-1.md)).

VLAN50 (`10.44.50.x`) is **retired**. A device returning from offline self-heals when
it gets a normal `10.44.x.x` DHCP lease — LAN Watcher picks it up within 5 minutes.

### Fire TV ADB pairing state

`adbkey.pub` pairs are physical-TV-bound. Prior to 2026-05-28, the TM
container's ADB key lived inside the container's writable layer and was
regenerated on every image rebuild — meaning every Stage 3D/3E/3F bump
silently broke every Fire TV pairing.

**Persistence fix (2026-05-28):** the TM container's ADB client
identity is now stored on hub2 at `/opt/charliehub/secrets/tm-adb/`
(host uid 1000, mode 700) and bind-mounted at `/home/appuser/.android`
via `docker-compose.yml`. Image rebuilds preserve the key; once a TV
accepts the prompt, the trust persists permanently. Pubkey sha256
`088b8f0d…0f5da8aa`, identifier shown on TV prompts as `@unknown`.

**Probe-exit defect fixed (2026-05-28):** `app/routers/tv_devices.py:178`
changed `| nc ifconfig.me 80` → `| toybox nc ifconfig.me 80`. Fire TV's
`/system/bin/sh` has no `nc` on PATH; the handler used to map the
resulting `nc: not found` failure to `adb_unreachable`, which was
indistinguishable from the (unrelated) auth-failure case.

ADB pairing is live operational state that changes on power-cycle / re-image — run `adb devices` on the host that currently hosts ADB for the real-time picture. The table below is a **historical snapshot (2026-05-28)**; note `adb` is no longer installed on px1 as of 2026-06-30, so the *px1 ADB* column is stale:

| TV | px1 ADB | TM container ADB | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kitchen | ✅ `device` | ⚠️ `unauthorized` | px1 canary subject |
| Master Bedroom | ✅ `device` | ⚠️ `unauthorized` | px1 canary subject |
| Paris | ✅ `device` (2026-05-28) | ✅ `device` (2026-05-28) | `/probe-exit` returns `84.102.220.13` |
| Dinard | ⚠️ `offline` | ⚠️ `unauthorized` | pair went stale; needs physical re-pair |
| Lounge | ❌ no route | — | currently unreachable |
| Snug | ❌ no route | — | VLAN50 retired; self-heals on reconnect |

Each `unauthorized` row needs a one-time "Allow USB debugging" prompt
accepted on the TV screen — after acceptance, all future rebuilds keep
the pairing. **Known diagnostic gap:** the handler runs
`adb -s <ip>:5555 shell …` without a prior `adb connect`. TVs not in
the daemon's connection table return "no such device" → mapped to
`adb_unreachable`. A pre-connect would surface the more actionable
`adb_unauthorized` signal — two-line follow-up, deferred.

The mutation chain (PUT/DELETE + realization) is unaffected by ADB
pair state; only the live probe button is degraded for un-paired TVs.

## Canal+ Installation

Canal+ requires special handling because it checks its installer source. A plain
sideload triggers an **"App Not Owned"** error.

### Install with Google Play installer flag

Use the `-i` flag to set the installer package to Google Play, which bypasses the
ownership check:

```bash
adb -s <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555 install -i com.android.vending /tmp/canal-plus.apk
```

!!! warning "Post-install behaviour"
    After installing with the `-i` flag, the Fire TV may redirect to the Amazon
    Appstore to re-download Canal+, and you may see a few errors during this process.
    This is expected — let it complete and Canal+ should work normally afterwards.

### Verify installer source

```bash
adb -s <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555 shell dumpsys package com.canal.android.canal | grep installerPackageName
```

Should show: `installerPackageName=com.android.vending`

### If "App Not Owned" persists

1. Uninstall Canal+: `adb -s <IP>:5555 uninstall com.canal.android.canal`
2. Reinstall with the `-i` flag as shown above
3. Ensure the VPN is connected to France before opening Canal+

## Keep-Awake / Disable Sleep

Fire TVs ship with an aggressive sleep timer that drops the device off the
network after a period of inactivity — which breaks the LAN-based geo routing
(LAN Watcher loses the lease) and the ADB probe-exit button. For always-on
units (e.g. Paris, Dinard) it is usually best to disable sleep entirely.

Connect via `adb connect <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555` from any machine, then:

```bash
# Never sleep
adb -s <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555 shell settings put secure sleep_timeout 0

# Disable the screensaver / screen-off
# 2147460000 ms ≈ 24 days — the value Amazon itself uses for "Never"
adb -s <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555 shell settings put system screen_off_timeout 2147460000
```

Verify the values stuck:

```bash
adb -s <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555 shell settings get secure sleep_timeout       # → 0
adb -s <FIRE_TV_IP>:5555 shell settings get system screen_off_timeout  # → 2147460000
```

To revert, set `sleep_timeout` back to a sane value (e.g. `1800000` = 30 min)
and `screen_off_timeout` to your preferred idle timeout.

!!! tip "adbLink GUI"
    The [adbLink](https://www.jocala.com/) desktop GUI exposes the same
    `sleep_timeout` change as a one-click **"Sleep off"** button if you prefer
    not to drop to the shell.

> Applied to **Fire TV Paris** (`10.75.1.174`) on 2026-05-29.

## Reserved sub-allocations

Per the [locality sub-allocation conventions](../network/fabric-v2/address-plan.md#locality-sub-allocation-conventions),
the FR locality `10.35.0.0/16` carves three canonical `/24` sub-ranges by
functional role:

| Subnet | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `10.35.1.0/24` | **Infrastructure plane** — fr-edge-1, px5, switches, APs, infra VMs | **active** — gateway `10.35.1.1` CCM-realized |
| `10.35.2.0/24` | **Human / user devices** | **active** — gateway `10.35.2.1` CCM-realized; DHCP scope live (pool `.100–.200`); **user devices are the default DHCP class** (unknown clients land here; infrastructure stays in `.1.x` via explicit reservation or static address) |
| `10.35.4.0/24` | **Managed consumers** — Fire TV Dinard (`10.35.4.10`), Apple TV Dinard (`10.35.4.11`), future media consumers | **active** — gateway `10.35.4.1` CCM-realized; static-only scope. Both reservations relocated 2026-07-27; each device adopts its `.4.x` address at next DHCP renewal (24 h lease) or on reboot. |

Third octets `.3`, `.5`, `.6`, … are **deliberately unassigned**. Adding
a new functional role requires doctrine update first.

These conventions are **operational legibility only**. Authority for
managed-consumer behavior lives in `tv_devices` + `routing_overrides` per
[I-GEO-CONSUMER-1](../control-plane/invariants/i-geo-consumer-1.md);
subnet membership is never an authority for routing or policy.

Managed by Transit Manager — do **not** hand-edit

### WAN / NAT

SFR Fibre, ONT cable terminated on fr-edge-1 `nic0`. fr-edge-1 performs
MASQUERADE on the WAN interface for all LAN-originated internet traffic.
NAT and policy-routing rules are generated by CCM Edge (edge_id 7) — do
not hand-edit `iptables` or `ip rule`.

The exact WAN IP is dynamic (SFR DHCP lease) and is not documented here
as architecture. Current public address is reflected via
`fr-vpn.charliehub.net` once DDNS is wired up post-cutover.

**WAN lease runtime (2026-07-13):** `ccm.edges.wan_runtime_enabled` flipped
`true` for edge_id 7 — closing a real gap: since May commissioning, the
dynamic SFR DHCP lease had no auto-reacquisition path if it lapsed

deploy attempt hit F-CCMEDGE-1 (`/usr/local/lib/charliehub/` didn't exist on

## Gateway — paris-edge-pi4

paris-edge-pi4 is the **sole** `wg-paris` peer on ch-transit-core. No other device at the Paris site has a gateway, WAN, DHCP, or NAT role.

### SSH access

```bash
ssh edge-fr2        # via SD-WAN transit (fabric path)
ssh edge-fr2-wan    # recovery path via public WAN (fleet recovery key)
```

### SD-WAN

`wg-site` on paris-edge-pi4 terminates the SD-WAN fabric to ch-transit-core. Managed by `charliehub-edge-agent` — do **not** hand-edit `/etc/wireguard/wg-site.conf`.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Local address | `10.244.75.2/30` |
| Peer | ch-transit-core `wg-paris` (`51.68.235.106:51875`) |
| Keepalive | 25 seconds |

The `wg-quick@wg-site.service` systemd unit is intentionally **disabled**. The edge agent (`charliehub-edge-agent.service`) owns the WireGuard lifecycle, with `charliehub-edge-reconcile.timer` as a 5-minute safety-net replay.

```bash
# Verify site tunnel from hub2
ssh root@10.0.0.2 'wg show wg-paris'    # transit-core side
ping -c3 10.75.1.1                       # Pi4 reachability
```

### WAN / NAT

SFR Fibre, ONT cable terminated directly on paris-edge-pi4 `nic0`. `dhclient` on `nic0` uses `vendor-class-identifier "neufbox_NB6VAC-FXC"` — required for the SFR ONT to issue a public DHCP lease. paris-edge-pi4 performs MASQUERADE on `nic0` for all LAN-originated internet traffic. NAT and policy-routing rules are generated by CCM Edge — do not hand-edit `nftables` or `ip rule`.

WAN IP `84.102.220.13` is stable (SFR DHCP). DDNS pushed to `paris-vpn.charliehub.net` every 5 min by `/usr/local/bin/charliehub-wan-push.sh`.

**AX88179 note:** `ethtool nic0` reports `Duplex: Half` — cosmetic driver limitation (`cdc_ncm` does not implement full link-mode reporting). Validated throughput: ~848 Mbps down / ~867 Mbps up.

`dnsmasq` on paris-edge-pi4 is the DHCP server for the Paris LAN. All scopes are CCM-LAN managed — do not hand-edit `/etc/dnsmasq.d/`.

### Out-of-band recovery — Comet KVM

When uk-edge-1 is unreachable over the network — a bad routing/NAT deploy, a PPPoE or LTE WAN failure, a kernel hang, or a boot that stalls before SSH comes up — recovery goes through **[uk-comet1](../reference/comet-uk.md)**, a GL.iNet GL-RM1 KVM-over-IP wired directly to this node's HDMI output and USB HID gadget. It is the dedicated out-of-band lifeline for uk-edge-1.

**By design**, the Comet is a physically separate recovery console — wired directly to uk-edge-1's HDMI + USB HID gadget, with its own LTE uplink (**Huawei E5885** hotspot) and its own `wg_oob` WireGuard tunnel to hub2 — reachable independently of uk-edge-1's WAN or fabric path. **Online as of 2026-07-26** (recovery-plane address `10.244.200.225/32`; auto-recovers `wg_oob` at boot over the E5885). The earlier Netgear LM1200 uplink was retired after it starved the Comet of DHCP at cold-boot — see [comet-uk.md](../reference/comet-uk.md). Its independence remains **conditional** on the Comet's own uplink, power and `wg_oob` tunnel — it is not unconditionally "independent of all networking". Day-to-day access is the web KVM at **`https://comet-kvm.charliehub.internal/`** (fabric-only, via hub2 Traefik).

See **[Comet KVM-over-IP (GL-RM1)](../reference/comet-uk.md)** for SSH access, the LTE modem admin tunnel, provisioning, and boot-survival details.
### Out-of-band config delivery — `wg-mgmt → px1 → charles@10.44.1.1`

When uk-edge-1's `wg-site` overlay is **down** (e.g. a `wg-uk` key split), neither
`POST /api/transit/deploy` (rides the dead overlay) nor `deploy-transit.sh` (skips the edge on its
mgmt-IP probe) can reach it — and the tunnel-rotation fix must be delivered **OOB**, not in-band over
the tunnel being fixed. The **proven** delivery path (validated during the 2026-07 wg-site key-split
outage) is via the independent `wg-mgmt` plane, hopping through px1:

```bash
# From hub2: wg-mgmt reaches the UK px cluster (10.244.150.x) independent of wg-uk.
# px1 (10.244.150.5) has LAN reach to the edge; charles@10.44.1.1 is a real sudo shell
# (root@10.44.1.1 lands in the restricted edge-dispatch ForceCommand).
hub2 → wg-mgmt → px1 (10.244.150.5) → charles@10.44.1.1
```

Deliver a corrected, `wg-site`-scoped render and apply it **non-bouncing** (`wg syncconf`, not
`wg-quick down/up`) so the `10.44.1.1` LAN path is never cut. Crucially, a live-kernel fix alone is
**not durable**: the edge-agent's local `edge-cached-artifact.json` is replayed every 5 min by
`charliehub-edge-reconcile.timer`, so you must also **refresh that cache** (quiesce the timer →
converge the tunnel → refresh cache via an overlay-delivered signed render → verify → release). See
the [2026-07 key-split postmortem](../operations/postmortems/2026-07-uk-wg-site-key-split.md) and
[Transit Reconcile & Verify](../operations/transit-reconcile-verify.md).

!!! note "OOB roles: the KVM is a console, wg-mgmt is the config-delivery path"
    The [Comet KVM](../reference/comet-uk.md) is a *console* lifeline (restored 2026-07-26 on its
    Huawei E5885 uplink) — but a console is not a config-delivery channel. During the 2026-07 wg-site
    key-split the `wg-mgmt → px1 → charles@` path above was the working channel for delivering config
    while the overlay was down. Treat `wg-mgmt` as the primary OOB **config-delivery** path and the
    KVM as the **console** fallback; verify KVM reachability before relying on it.

# USA Site (Philadelphia)

**Lifecycle:** OPERATION

**UCG Ultra** — USA GEO exit node for the B2 fabric-native peer model.

!!! abstract "Filed under sites/ — but USA is a service, not an SD-WAN site"
    USA is a **GEO Exit Provider** — a *service transport* per [I-IFACE-DOMAIN-1](../control-plane/invariants/i-iface-domain-1.md), not a fabric site. Its entire role is one capability: **US egress**, via the appliance-realized `wga-usa` interface. It has no LAN, no Linux edge, no DNS or control-plane authority, and does not participate in fabric routing. This page lives under `sites/` only because that is where operators look for it; the *transport-domain* classification (service, not fabric) is what governs how it is managed. See the Architectural Invariant directly below.

---

## Architectural Invariant — Appliance Egress Target by Design

!!! warning "Read this before proposing any changes to the USA site"

    **USA is an appliance egress target by design.** It is intentionally and permanently asymmetric with UK and FR. Do not attempt to normalise it.

    USA is **not**, and must never become:

    - A **CCM Linux edge** — there is no Linux node to push kernel state to. The UCG is a UniFi appliance; CCM's render/apply model does not apply.
    - A **LAN authority** — there is no USA LAN. No DHCP scopes, no CCM-LAN records, no dnsmasq.
    - A **DNS authority** — no dnsmasq, no resolver, no split-horizon. USA peers resolve via hub2 (`10.0.0.1` / `10.254.0.1`) over the fabric tunnel, same as every other peer.
    - A **control-plane node** — no Transit Manager instance, no Domain Manager instance, no Docs API, no Prometheus scrape target. hub2 is the sole control-plane host.
    - An **SD-WAN site** — there is no USA LAN segment, no wg-site, no site gateway IP, no CCM edge node record. The UCG is a GEO exit peer, not a site gateway.

    The asymmetry is intentional. UK and FR are full SD-WAN sites with Linux edge nodes, LAN management, and kernel enforcement. USA exists solely to provide a US public IP for fabric peers assigned `geo=us`. Its entire role is: terminate a WireGuard tunnel from transit-core, NAT egress traffic through the UCG's WAN.

    **Any proposal that would add LAN management, DNS authority, CCM edge registration, or SD-WAN site semantics to the USA site is out of scope by doctrine.** If the requirement genuinely exists, open a design discussion — do not extend the existing USA configuration.

| Rock server endpoint | `us-vpn.charliehub.net:51820` |

## Role

The UCG provides a USA public IP for fabric peers assigned `geo=us`. All three exit
infrastructures (UK PPPoE edge, FR Dinard edge, USA Rock/UCG) are exercised through
identical peer semantics — only `peer.geo` changes, not the tunnel or identity.

## Architecture (B2 — 2026-05-14)

Transit-core is a **WireGuard client** of the UCG's `wgsrv1` Rock server.
Traffic flow for a peer with `geo=us`:

```
fabric peer (10.99.x) → wg-rw on transit-core
  → ip rule pref 5000+peer_id from 10.99.x lookup geo-us
  → ip route table 203: default dev wga-usa
  → nft masquerade: saddr 10.99.0.0/16 oifname wga-usa → source becomes 192.168.4.10
  → WireGuard wga-usa sends encrypted to us-vpn.charliehub.net:51820 (Rock server)
  → UCG wgsrv1 decrypts, forwards out WAN, NATs to 98.115.202.204
```

No DNAT rule on hub2 is required — transit-core initiates outbound, not inbound.
No `UBIOS_WAN_WAN_USER` firewall rule required — wgsrv1 clients are NAT'd through
WAN by default in UniFi's WireGuard server implementation.

## WireGuard Tunnels

### wga-usa — GEO exit tunnel — client mode

Transit-core connects to UCG's Rock server as a WireGuard client. The interface name
`wga-usa` encodes: `wg` (WireGuard) + `a` (appliance-realized, i.e. not CCM-managed)
+ `usa` (site). This distinguishes it from `wg-uk`, `wg-fr`, `wg-paris` which are
Linux-edge tunnels under Transit Manager's render-deploy cycle.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| WireGuard public keys | **Not pinned here** — `wga-usa` is appliance-realized; kernel↔intent pubkey drift is detected by [I-IFACE-HEALTH-1](../control-plane/invariants/i-iface-health-1.md) (WARN-only). Read live: `wg show wga-usa` on transit-core, or the UniFi UI (VPN → WireGuard). |
| Rock server endpoint | `us-vpn.charliehub.net:51820` |
| transit-core tunnel IP | `192.168.4.10/32` |
| AllowedIPs (peer→Rock) | `0.0.0.0/0` — all geo-us traffic exits via Rock |
| PersistentKeepalive | 25s (transit-core side) |
| Table | `off` — routes managed by Transit Manager policy tables, not WireGuard |

Config file on transit-core: `/etc/wireguard/wga-usa.conf` (post-T3 placement, outside `generated/`)
Private key: `/etc/wireguard/keys/wga-usa.key`

### wgsrv1 — UCG Rock WireGuard Server

UCG-managed WireGuard server. Transit-core is a client peer.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| UCG pubkey | Read live from the UniFi UI (VPN → WireGuard) or `wg show` — not pinned (appliance-realized; see [I-IFACE-HEALTH-1](../control-plane/invariants/i-iface-health-1.md)). |
| transit-core peer IP | `192.168.4.10/32` |
| Server subnet | `192.168.4.0/24` |
| Listen port | `51820` |

Managed via the UniFi UI. Transit-core's peer was added by importing
`Rock-Wireguard-server-charliehub-transit-core-us.conf` (generated by UCG,
saved at `px3:/tmp/` during B2 sprint).

## Failure Recovery

If `wg show wga-usa` shows no recent handshake:

1. Check Rock server is reachable: `nc -vzu us-vpn.charliehub.net 51820`
2. Check wga-usa is up on transit-core: `systemctl status wg-quick@wga-usa`
3. Restart if needed: `systemctl restart wg-quick@wga-usa` — transit-core will reconnect within 25s (PersistentKeepalive). This also re-resolves the endpoint hostname, which is needed if the UCG WAN IP has rotated since the tunnel last came up.
4. Check UCG is online and Rock server is running (UniFi UI → VPN → WireGuard)

All commands above run on transit-core (10.0.0.2) via:
```bash
ssh hub2 "ssh -T -i /opt/charliehub/secrets/transit_id_ed25519 root@transit-core.charliehub.internal '<command>'"
```

## WAN Push

The UCG self-reports its WAN IP every 5 minutes via `/data/wan-push/site-wan-push.sh`,
installed as a system cron at `/etc/cron.d/wan-push`:

```
UCG cron (/data/wan-push/site-wan-push.sh)
 → HTTPS POST to ddns.charliehub.net/api/ddns/update/us-vpn.charliehub.net
 → OVH DNS updated (TTL ~100s)
```

The DDNS record is consumed by [WAN IP Watcher](../infrastructure/wan-ip-watcher.md), which propagates the current IP to Traefik allowlists, Authelia, and the hub2 SSH nftables (UK/FR/Paris only — USA is not in the SSH allowlist). The hostname stays stable across UCG WAN IP rotations; downstream consumers re-resolve via DoH every ~5 minutes.

The `wga-usa` tunnel uses `us-vpn.charliehub.net` as its WireGuard endpoint; `wg-quick` resolves it at interface bringup. If the UCG WAN IP rotates while the tunnel is up, the client will continue sending to the old IP until `wg-quick@wga-usa` is restarted — see [Failure Recovery](#failure-recovery).

## Gate 4 Proof (2026-05-14)

Full geo mutation cycle — uk → fr → local → us → uk — with **wg0 handshake age strictly increasing** throughout. Proves identity stability under live policy mutation with zero tunnel flaps.

| Step | wg0 handshake age | Exit IP |
|------|-------------------|---------| 
| baseline: uk | 1m 04s | `93.89.136.208` (UK) |
| after uk → fr | 1m 15s | `78.116.21.175` (FR, SFR Dinard) |
| after fr → local | 1m 29s | FAIL — no exit rule (expected) |
| after local → us | 1m 51s | `98.115.202.204` (USA, UCG WAN at the time of test) |
| after us → uk | 2m 01s | `93.89.136.208` (UK) |

Same peer (`10.99.0.2`, peer 95), same WireGuard session, same tunnel, same keys.
Only `peer.geo` and the runtime `ip rule` changed. No `deploy-transit.sh`, no edge deploy, no restart.

## Known Gap — LAN/TV consumers cannot use this exit yet (Phase 3b)

Today only **road-warrior peers** (`peers.geo=us`) reach this exit. LAN/TV
consumers (`routing_overrides` / `tv.charliehub.net`) set to `geo=us` have **no
realization path**: `transit.geo_executors` has no `geo=us` row, and because USA
is an appliance egress target (no Linux edge), an edge-local executor cannot be
added per-site. The fix is **central execution on transit-core** for
central-only geos, tracked as I-EXEC-US-1 (Phase 3b). See
[GEO Consumer Convergence — Appendix A](../network/fabric-v2/geo-consumer-convergence.md)
for the full design.
